verses.note: God binds his future actions to a visible sign and speaks of remembering it. The language is deliberately human, but the point is his faithfulness: God places his own word where he will see it and pledges to act according to it.

The verse shows God's patience. He waits four centuries rather than act before judgment is just, which is the same forbearance the New Testament describes as meant to lead to repentance (Romans 2:4, 2 Peter 3:9).
God's faithfulness is shown here as the exact match between what he says and what he does. The verse repeats the point twice so that no reader can miss that the birth is the keeping of a word.
